summary: The study investigates the properties of three different ALD-W thin films as nucleation layers for W-plug deposition in 70 nm design-rule DRAM. The films were deposited using alternating exposures of WF6 and SiH4, or WF6 and B2H6. The films showed excellent step coverage but high resistivity due to impurities and phase structures. The B2H6-based ALD-W film formed an amorphous phase, leading to lower resistivity and stable contact resistance at ultrahigh aspect ratio contacts.
evidence: The properties of three different kinds of atomic-layer-deposited W thin films were comparatively characterized and investigated as nucleation layers for the W-plug process of 70 nm design-rule dynamic random access memory. ALD-W film was deposited using alternating exposures of WF6 and SiH4, and another film was treated with B2H6 prior to W ALD using WF6 and SiH4. Finally, ALD-W film was deposited using alternating exposures of WF6 and B2H6. All the ALD-W films showed excellent step coverage at the contact with an aspect ratio of 15, but their resistivities were as high as 125–145 Ω·cm at the thickness of 20 nm. High resistivities of ALD-W films are discussed on the basis of impurities cooperation such as Si and B, phase (body-centered-cubic W or primitive cubic W), crystallinity (crystalline or amorphous), and grain size. It was found that ALD-W film formed an amorphous phase, which was stable until 900°C annealing. This is clearly different from ALD-W with polycrystalline grains of W and W was transformed to W after 800°C annealing. The formation of amorphous W resulted in the formation of large-size grains of chemical-vapor-deposited W film deposited on ALD-W and the reduction in the resistivity of W-plug stack. The integration results showed that the reduced resistivity of W-plug stack with ALD-W provided a significantly lower resistance at the W bit line contact. Another advantage of the integration scheme with ALD-W was its stable contact resistance at the ultrahigh aspect ratio contact even though the step coverage of the underlayer, TiN, was poor. It was also found that the B2H6 pretreatment was effective for obtaining the low and stable contact resistance at UHAR contact.
